properties.areaDesc: Buncombe, NC; Henderson, NC
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 10 at 11:29AM EDT until October 12 at 2:00PM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
...The Flood Advisory continues for the following rivers in North
Carolina...

French Broad River Near at Old Fanning Bridge Rd, 3 W Fletcher
affecting Henderson and Buncombe Counties.

.Tropical rain showers will continue to overspread the mountains
through tonight becoming increasingly heavy, leading to excessive
runoff and rises on streams within the upper French Broad River
watershed.  Storm-total rainfall of 4-8 inches is expected, with
isolated 8-10 inches possible within the upper French Broad River
watershed, generally upstream of Etowah.  The highest totals will
occur along the Tanassee and Pisgah ridges, with lesser amounts
within the upper French Broad River valley.  Additionally, 4-6 inches
of rainfall are expected within the Mud Creek watershed in Henderson
County, which is a primary tributary of the French Broad River above
Fletcher.  While there continues to be some uncertainty regarding the
exact location, timing, and amounts of the heaviest rainfall, there
is enough confidence in the current forecast that out-of-bank
conditions are likely for the upper French Broad River. This rise
above Action Stage will result in nuisance, relatively shallow
flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to the French Broad River,
including farmland, woodlands, low-lying secondary roads, greenways,
parks, and other flood-prone locations.

More significant rises along the French Broad River are possible, and
those with interests along the river are encouraged to stay weather
aware and up-to-date on the latest stream levels and forecasts at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/GSP.  Current reasonable worst-case
scenarios are posted in the ADDITIONAL DETAILS sections below.
Forecast crests above Minor Flood Stage may result in the River Flood
Advisories being upgraded to River Flood Warnings.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...French Broad River near at Old Fanning Bridge Rd, 3 W
Fletcher.

* WHEN...Until Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 10.0 feet, Action/Advisory Stage.  The French Broad
River has exceeded bankfull at the gauge site.  Isolated farmland
flooding is beginning across the French Broad River Valley from
Etowah downstream to Avery Creek upstream of the gauge site.

* At 11.5 feet, Action Stage Flooding continues.  Butler Bridge Rd.
is inundated with up to 6 inches of floodwaters from the French
Broad River, forcing road closure.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:30 AM EDT Saturday the stage was 3.8 feet and rising.
- Bankfull stage is 10.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 10.6 feet
early tomorrow afternoon.  A crest closer to 12 feet is possible.
A reasonable worst-case crest above Minor Flood Stage below 15
feet cannot be ruled out.
- Action stage is 10.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 13.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

For detailed information including observed and forecast stages,
flood impacts, flood history, FEMA Flood Hazard Layers, and more,
please visit: https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/GSP

The next statement should be issued this evening before 1130 PM EDT.

properties.areaDesc: Holmes, FL; Washington, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 10 at 11:09AM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in Florida...

Choctawhatchee River near Caryville (US 90) affecting Holmes and
Washington Counties.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Choctawhatchee River near Caryville (US 90).

* WHEN...From Monday evening until further notice.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:00 AM CDT Saturday the stage was 7.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 9.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
Monday evening and continue rising to a crest of 15.2 feet early
Wednesday afternoon.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 15.2
feet on 03/06/1991.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1000 PM CDT.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING IN EFFECT FROM MONDAY EVENING UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE
